real_name: Film character named after a militant — not the Palestinian leader
naming_note: The character name 'Yasir Arafat' in the film does NOT refer to Yasser Arafat (1929-2004), Chairman of the PLO/Palestinian Authority. The film's naming is a deliberate reference to Pakistani jihadist culture: naming sons after Palestinian and pan-Islamic figures was common in militant circles in Pakistan through the 1980s-2000s. 'Yasir Arafat' as a Pakistani name appears in multiple LeT and JeM operative lists. The film uses this to signal the character's jihadist ideological roots without making him a specific real-world individual.
real_life_notes: Composite character — represents the middle-tier Pakistani militant who has been ideologically formed by the Afghan jihad era (1980s), indoctrinated through Muridke-style madrassa pipelines, and deployed operationally by LeT/JeM into the ISI's Karachi infrastructure. This archetype is heavily documented: fighters who are not household-name leaders but constitute the operational backbone of Pakistani militant groups.
film_role: Film 1/2 — ISI-linked militant operative; likely connected to either the LeT network (Azam Cheema/Bhuttovi chain) or the Karachi-based JeM infrastructure (Zahoor Mistry/Ibrahim Athar chain). His role is mid-level operational: couriers, safe house management, logistics for militant movement — the unglamorous connective tissue that makes terror operations possible.
objective: Execute ISI-assigned operational tasks; maintain militant safe house network; facilitate movement of operatives and materiel; avoid Indian and Western surveillance

ideological_formation.naming_tradition: Named after pan-Islamic figure — common in Pakistani jihadist families from 1980s-90s
ideological_formation.indoctrination_pathway: Madrassa → LeT/JeM Muridke-style camp → ISI operational deployment
ideological_formation.motivation: Mix of religious ideology, financial incentive, and organisational loyalty — not a true believer martyr (that's Kasab's archetype); rather a careerist operative
